---
title: "Migrating from version 3: the sampleMetadata map"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(curatedMetagenomicData)
library(dplyr)
extdata <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "curatedMetagenomicData")
columns <- read.csv(extdata("cmd3_to_cmd4_columns.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
values <- read.csv(extdata("cmd3_to_cmd4_values.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
conditions <- read.csv(extdata("cmd3_to_cmd4_conditions.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
show <- function(x) DT::datatable(x, options = list(pageLength = 25), rownames = FALSE, extensions = "Responsive")
```

Version 4 keeps the name `sampleMetadata` but its columns follow the cMD 4 data
dictionary, so a version 3 script that filters on a renamed or recoded column
needs updating. This page is the complete map, derived from the curation
repository, which keeps the same 22,588 samples in both schemas. Three CSV files
in the package's `extdata` directory hold it, and the tables below render them.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
system.file("extdata", "cmd3_to_cmd4_columns.csv", package = "curatedMetagenomicData")
system.file("extdata", "cmd3_to_cmd4_values.csv", package = "curatedMetagenomicData")
system.file("extdata", "cmd3_to_cmd4_conditions.csv", package = "curatedMetagenomicData")
```

They are regenerated by `data-raw/cmd3_to_cmd4_map.R`, which joins the last
version 3 `sampleMetadata` to the version 4 table on `study_name` and
`sample_id`, checks every column decision against the data, and derives the
value maps.

# Columns

Every version 3 column, with the version 4 column or columns that hold its
values and how they relate:

| relation | meaning |
|---|---|
| `same` | same name, same values |
| `renamed` | new name, same values |
| `recoded` | same name, values changed; see the value map |
| `renamed+recoded` | both |
| `restructured` | several columns replace it; the notes say how |
| `biomarker` | packed into `biomarker_name`, `biomarker_unit` and `biomarker_value` (aligned `;`-separated lists); the notes give the `biomarker_name` entry |
| `uncurated` | packed into `uncurated_metadata` as `name:value` |
| `dropped` | not carried into version 4 |

`coverage` is the share of samples with a version 3 value that have a value in
the first version 4 column named; `identical` is the share of those whose
values are equal, for `same` and `renamed` rows.

```{r}
table(columns$relation)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(columns)
```

Three changes affect most scripts.

- **Read counts** (`number_reads`, `number_bases`) are no longer curated. They
  come from the release's QC table and appear as `number_reads`,
  `reads_decontaminated` and `bases_decontaminated` in the `colData` of
  returned objects.
- **Age** is `age` in the unit given by `age_unit` (Year, Month or Day), with
  `age_years` always in years; `infant_age` in days is folded in the same way.
  `age_group` is re-derived from `age_years`, so it does not map one to one onto
  the old `age_category`.
- **Lab values** moved from one column each (`hdl`, `hba1c`, `creatinine`, ...)
  to the three aligned `biomarker_*` list columns; to get one back, split
  `biomarker_name` and `biomarker_value` on `;` and pick the position whose name
  matches. The same measurement is spelled two ways across studies
  (`Cholesterol` and `Cholesterol Measurement`), so match on both.

# Values

For every recoded column with a manageable number of levels, each observed pair
of old and new values with its count. `NA` in the new value means the old value
was not carried over for those samples.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(values)
```

Two mappings to note: `non_westernized` becomes `westernized` with the sense
inverted, and `smoker` becomes one or more SNOMED finding names, so filter with
`grepl("Smoker \\(finding\\)", smoker)` rather than an equality test.

# Conditions

Version 3 described a sample's condition with `study_condition` (what the
study compared) and `disease` (what the participant had). Version 4 uses three
columns: `target_condition`, the condition or conditions the study targets;
`control`, which is `Case`, `Study Control` or `Not Used`; and `disease`, the
participant's conditions as ontology names. The map is per study, because the
same `study_condition` value means different things in different studies.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(conditions)
```

A version 3 filter such as `disease == "healthy"` becomes `control == "Study
Control"` when you mean the study's controls, or `disease == "Healthy"` when you
mean participants with no recorded condition; the two are not the same set.
